items.title: Manuel Joseph "Moose" Zanco Interview, 1959-11-25
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Emile Barnes; the mention is made solely by the interviewer.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's an old time thing. All the guys, tell me they used to do that. I've heard Emile Barnes and, uh, Albert Burbank together. They didn't have a trumpet play at one time, you know. And I sat in on the trombone. Yeah. And it was fun, you know, to hear them play like that. It sounded good. And John Handy and Willie Humphrey used to do that, too. Yeah.

Well, I don't think, uh, you'll see too many of the bands around the city now that do anything like that. No. I mean, it's just a novelty with us. Another thing, you hardly will see a banjo in your bands anymore. You see, or a toolbar, as far as that goes. You don't see things like that anymore. So I think that's what we are more or less capitalizing on, is the fact that we are reproducing the old, the real old sound, see. And, uh, that's what's keeping us going.
